data.name: Counter Agents
data.detailed_description:
Check out ConSPYration! Made my the Devs who brought you Counter Agents!



Counter Agents is a spy-themed, head-to-head multiplayer game where your objective is to sneak around guards, steal the briefcase, and make it to an exit point before your opponent. Take on the solo-player challenges, compete with your friends in multiplayer mode, and enjoy creating your own maps with the brilliantly simple level editor!

Counter Agents originally started as a student program prototype project during the Fall of 2015 and gradually took shape to what it is today. The original goal was to take an arcade game dating 1983 or earlier and build off of existing mechanics to create something new and unique. The game we were inspired by was 005 (1981), one of the very first stealth games. Of the various 005 game modes, we loved the scenes where you had to avoid policemen with flashlights. We took this idea and created a customizable multiplayer experience with more 3D levels. Keeping the project alive between projects, we have playtested, iterated and polished Counter Agents tirelessly over the past year. Now we’re excited to finally bring it to Steam!

Key Features:

  • Three game modes include Single Player Challenge, Multiplayer (1-4 players), and Level Editor. The goal of each mode is to find and steal a briefcase and escape, all while avoiding guards, detectives, and other players.
  • Top-down view of a 3D environment. There are 3 floors that promote clever level design and strategy.
  • Level editor has a simple UI with a drag and drop mechanic so that anyone can create complex designs. Players can post levels to the online community for anyone to play and rate.
  • All original music and audio by our composer, Lance Montgomery.
  • Counter Agents will be completely free! No in-game purchases, and no priced DLC.

reviews.review:
Counter Agents is a multiplayer stealth game that takes inspiration from classic espionage concepts and transforms them into a competitive experience focused on deception, awareness, and clever movement. Developed by James Montgomery, Daniel Paez, Jeff Jackman, Lance Montgomery, and Michael Nova, and published by Counter_Agents_Team, the game originated as a student project before becoming a fully released title on Steam. Its premise is straightforward but effective: players compete to locate a briefcase and successfully escape while avoiding security forces and outmaneuvering rival agents pursuing the same objective.

Rather than relying on direct firefights or traditional action mechanics, Counter Agents emphasizes stealth as its primary gameplay pillar. Every match encourages players to think carefully about their movements, monitor patrol routes, and remain aware of other competitors. The constant tension of sneaking through guarded areas while knowing that another player could reach the objective first creates an engaging dynamic. Success often comes not from quick reflexes alone but from patience, observation, and the ability to predict how opponents will behave.

One of the game's most interesting qualities is how it merges stealth gameplay with competitive multiplayer. Many stealth titles focus exclusively on single-player experiences, but Counter Agents adapts the formula into a contest where multiple participants are trying to achieve the same goal. This creates memorable situations where players may choose to remain hidden, race toward an objective, or intentionally mislead others. The human element adds unpredictability that artificial intelligence alone cannot provide, making each match feel different from the last.

The map design plays a significant role in maintaining variety. Levels are built around multiple floors, giving players access to vertical routes that can be used for escape, ambushes, or strategic positioning. This additional layer of navigation makes exploration more engaging and rewards those who learn the layout of each environment. Experienced players can take advantage of alternative paths and shortcuts, while newcomers gradually discover more efficient routes through repeated play.

Although multiplayer is clearly the centerpiece, the game also includes a challenge mode designed for solo play. These missions provide an opportunity to learn the mechanics and understand the behavior of guards before entering competitive matches. The mode serves as an effective training ground while also offering additional content for players who prefer to practice independently. It helps ease the learning curve and makes the overall package feel more complete.

The inclusion of a level editor significantly expands the game's longevity. Players are given tools to design their own environments through a user-friendly creation system, allowing the community to contribute fresh content. The ability to create, share, and rate custom maps keeps the experience from becoming stale and encourages experimentation. For a free-to-play title, this feature adds considerable value and demonstrates a commitment to replayability.

Visually, Counter Agents adopts a clean and functional presentation. The graphics are not designed to compete with large-budget productions, but they effectively communicate important gameplay information. Characters, objectives, and environmental elements are easy to distinguish, which is particularly important in a stealth-focused game where situational awareness is critical. The colorful aesthetic also helps give the game a lighthearted personality that separates it from more serious espionage titles.

Sound design contributes positively to the overall atmosphere. Music and sound effects help establish the spy-themed setting while also providing useful feedback during gameplay. Players can use audio cues to identify nearby activity, making sound an important component of the stealth experience. While the soundtrack is not the game's main attraction, it supports the action effectively and enhances immersion.

Perhaps the most impressive aspect of Counter Agents is how much creativity it extracts from a relatively simple concept. The objective remains consistent, but the interaction between guards, detectives, environmental layouts, and competing players generates a wide variety of outcomes. Matches often produce unexpected moments of tension and excitement, whether that involves narrowly avoiding detection, stealing victory from another player, or escaping just seconds before capture.

The game's biggest challenge is its reliance on an active multiplayer environment. While the challenge mode offers some content for solo players, the core experience is built around human competition. Those looking for a narrative-driven adventure or a progression-heavy online game may find the offering somewhat limited. However, players who appreciate unique multiplayer concepts and stealth-oriented gameplay will likely find a great deal to enjoy.

Counter Agents succeeds because it understands its strengths and focuses on delivering a focused, entertaining experience. Its combination of stealth mechanics, competitive objectives, vertical map design, and community-generated content creates a game that feels distinctive even within a crowded multiplayer market. What began as a student project ultimately evolved into an enjoyable and inventive title that showcases how creative ideas can thrive without requiring a massive budget.

Rating: 8/10
